original_metadata.title: Five minimal four-hyperbolic-gamma integral representations of the relativistic conical function for positive step sizes, real arguments and coupling strictly between zero and their sum
original_metadata.author: Simon Ruijsenaars
original_metadata.source_title: A Relativistic Conical Function and its Whittaker Limits
original_metadata.difficulty_reason: The four-factor integral must be identified with the previously defined eight-factor relativistic conical function, rather than merely evaluated at special parameters. The author proves a hyperbolic kernel identity, shifts contours to derive joint difference equations, supplies the gamma-ratio Fourier transform through two incommensurable shift recurrences, and combines normalization with meromorphic uniqueness. These analytic and modular-double constructions exceed ordinary qualifying-examination special-function manipulations.

proof_review.note: Selected main minimal-integral representation (3.47), with the four equivalent Fourier forms (3.48)-(3.51) consolidated as the same result, for a_plus,a_minus>0, a=(a_plus+a_minus)/2, 0<b<2a, real x,y. R is the A1 specialization (1.2) of the previously defined BC1 function, with its actual eight-factor contour definition (2.1)-(2.8) retained. Read all new Section3 kernel/Fourier/contour construction17-22, including the special d=0 kernel identity, pole-free small-b shift strip, Plancherel decomposition, analytic continuation, normalization, joint eigenvalue equations and final identification. Full PropositionC.1 gamma-ratio Fourier transform48-51 is included as uncounted local support: shift recurrences in y and parameter difference, irrational-period proportionality, analytic continuation and elementary cosh normalization. Section2.3 uniqueness comparison13-14 retained; published Ruijsenaars1999 Section1 meromorphic-difference uniqueness and earlier R-function analyticity/eigenfunction theory I-III are explicitly cited background, not reconstructed. Hyperbolic gamma definitions, poles, asymptotics, reflection/duplication and residue43-45 retained with original references. The author explicitly identifies remaining residue cancellation as routine after all pole locations/ratios are printed; no omitted new kernel or transform core. No unitarity theorem, asymptotic strengthening, nonrelativistic or Whittaker/Toda limits counted; these have additional unreviewed obligations. Exact formulas and source notation preserved; no AI algebra repair. Exact selected statement and terminal proof pages rendered and visually inspected; all physical header/native ZIP members and source/license hashes checked. Scope and author routine-detail wording preserved; no independent mathematical reproof.
